nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Industry, innovation and infrastructure|Infrastructure financing|Public subsidies_qna_000
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: How do non-cooperative taxes and subsidies compare to first-best policies?
nodes.answer: Non-cooperative taxes are lower, while non-cooperative subsidies are higher compared to first-best policies.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Industry, innovation and infrastructure|Infrastructure financing|Public subsidies_qna_001
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What is the consequence of excessive subsidies in the context of the paper?
nodes.answer: Excessive subsidies mitigate the distortionary effect of inefficiently low emission taxes, but the equilibrium level of pollution remains inefficiently high.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Industry, innovation and infrastructure|Infrastructure financing|Public subsidies_qna_002
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What is the impact of high environmental subsidies according to the paper?
nodes.answer: High environmental subsidies mitigate the distortion of low taxes but lead to an inefficiently high equilibrium level of pollution.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Industry, innovation and infrastructure|Infrastructure financing|Public subsidies_qna_003
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: What is the main focus of the paper regarding public policy finance for energy subsidies?
nodes.answer: The paper evaluates common methods of energy subsidy cost-recovery, specifically a flat-rate household levy and an electricity price surcharge, considering both equity and efficiency effects.
